html:
The Battle of Mu'tah was fought in 629 near the village of Mu'tah, east of the Dead Sea in today's Jordan, between a Muslim army sent by Muhammad and the forces of the Byzantine Empire and its Arab allies.

The Muslims were heavily outnumbered. Their three commanders, Zayd ibn Haritha, Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, were killed one after another. Khalid ibn al-Walid took command and led a fighting retreat, for which he was called the Sword of God.

It was the first clash between Muslims and the Roman world. A few years later the Arab conquests took the whole region, after the Battle of the Yarmuk in 636. Shrines to the fallen commanders stand near the site.
